newsitem.title: USA: Local manufacturers less optimistic -- Phila. Fed.
newsitem.headline: Local manufacturers less optimistic -- Phila. Fed.

text.p: Local manufacturers in the U.S. third economic region appear to be less optimistic about growth prospects, said an official at Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia.

"This month we did see a reduction in optimism on the (part of) manufacturers over the next six months," Philadelphia Fed economist Michael Trebing told reporters after the bank's manufacturing survey for May was released.
The Philadelphia Fed business activity index dropped to 1.6 in May from 5.7 in the previous month.
Trebing also said auto strikes over the last few weeks at some U.S. car companies did not have a major effect on the findings of the Philadelphia survey for May.
"We received no special commentary this time on the impact of the strike...It's a minor component that this index measures," Trebing said.
The Philadelphia Fed economist also said the May survey indicated employment continued to grow in the region.
"We have more firms reporting increases in employment than reporting declines...We're continuing to see some growth in employment overall," Trebing said.
Philadelphia Fed serves the third U.S. economic district, which includes Delaware, the eastern region of Pennsylvania and the southern portion of New Jersey.
